- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks: Not recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary of key clinical findings, reasoning, and impressions from both transcript and DDx:
  - Presentation: ~1 week history of visible swelling at the tip of the left elbow (olecranon), noticed in shower. Patient reports minimal pain (“not painful at all” / “feels a bit weird”), slight warmth over the swelling, palpable fluid-like quality, preserved range of motion, no systemic symptoms (no fever, malaise).
  - Clinician assessment: favors olecranon bursitis (non-septic) based on local findings and preserved joint function; does not appear to be septic arthritis at presentation.
  - DDx concordant with clinician: highest likelihood assigned to aseptic olecranon bursitis; medium likelihood for septic bursitis/cellulitis and gout-related bursitis.
- Relevant differentials from DDx that support/refine clinician impression:
  - Aseptic (non-septic) olecranon bursitis — High likelihood (matches clinical exam and doctor’s impression).
  - Septic olecranon bursitis/localized cellulitis — Medium likelihood (possible given warmth; less likely due to absence of systemic signs and minimal tenderness).
  - Gout-related bursitis/crystal arthropathy — Medium likelihood (clinician plans gout testing; less likely given minimal pain and no prior gout history).
- Working diagnosis:
  - Aseptic (non-septic) olecranon bursitis of the left elbow — supported by local fluid-like swelling, slight warmth, preserved range of motion, and clinician assessment; consistent with DDx (High likelihood).
- Considerations (additional plausible but uncertain options from DDx):
  - Septic olecranon bursitis / localized cellulitis (monitor for progression of pain, spreading erythema, systemic features).
  - Gout-related bursitis/crystal arthropathy (gout testing planned).
  - Less likely: benign soft-tissue mass, traumatic hematoma or repetitive-pressure bursitis (patient denies trauma; no anticoagulant use recorded).
- Management plan documented in transcript:
  - Start ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food; stop if heartburn develops.
  - Arrange blood tests (inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, gout screen) — forms to be posted to patient; results expected in ~5–6 days.
  - Arrange follow-up after blood tests; follow-up may be face-to-face, phone, or video per patient preference.
  - Safety netting: return urgently (video/phone or in-person) if elbow becomes very red, very painful, redness spreads, or systemic symptoms develop (signs concerning for infection/septic bursitis).
- Conflict noted: None between transcript and DDx.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification: Patient encouraged to remain active; clinician advised how to take ibuprofen (take after food, watch for heartburn). No broader chronic disease prevention counseling recorded.
- Patient health goals and priorities: Patient reports being “fit and healthy” and runs regularly; no explicit health goals documented.
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA): Not recorded.
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports): Not recorded.
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled: Follow-up planned after blood test results; can be phone, video, or in-person per patient choice; timing contingent on blood test completion and results (~5–6 days).

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral: Not recorded.
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management: Not recorded (specialist referral not documented; may be considered if tests suggest rheumatologic disease or if infection/complexity arises).
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified: Not recorded.
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening: Not recorded.
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected: Not recorded.
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health: Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Aseptic (non-septic) olecranon bursitis — High likelihood. Justification: Localized fluid-like swelling at left olecranon with slight warmth, minimal pain, preserved range of motion, and clinician explicitly diagnosed bursitis.
- Septic olecranon bursitis / localized cellulitis — Medium likelihood. Justification: Local warmth and swelling could indicate infection, but absence of systemic signs, minimal tenderness, and clinician impression lower probability at present.
- Gout-related bursitis / crystal arthropathy — Medium likelihood. Justification: Acute localized inflammatory swelling at a bursal site is compatible with crystal arthropathy; clinician plans gout testing despite patient reporting minimal pain and no prior gout history.

Quality checks
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs (temperature, BP, pulse), anthropometry (height, weight, BMI), immunisation review, documented medication list (pre-existing), tobacco/alcohol/substance use details, renal/liver baseline tests explicitly listed, urinalysis, and any aspiration/culture of bursal fluid (not performed).
- Internal conflicts or contradictions between transcript and DDx: None identified.
- Transcript quality notes: Transcript appears complete for the encounter; occasional brief pauses and incomplete sentences present but clinical content is clear and sufficient for documentation.
